scope: Selective audit prompts for Articles 9-15, Annex IV, Article 50 and associated actor duties; grouped references are explicit and this is not an exhaustive EU AI Act catalog.

source.accessNote: EUR-Lex challenges automated clients; automated source checks read the same Official Journal documents from the Publications Office (CELLAR) access URLs.

applicationContext.legalSource: Article 113, third paragraph, point (c)(i) and (ii), as replaced by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, Art 1, point (40)(b)
applicationContext.covers: Chapter III Sections 1, 2 and 3 except Article 6(5)
applicationContext.approvalRule: Dates inform review; they do not automatically approve applicability. Assess Articles 2 and 111, route, actor, intended use, relevant modifications and sectoral rules. Article 111(2), as replaced: for high-risk systems placed on the market or put into service before the Chapter III date of their route (2 December 2027 for Annex III, 2 August 2028 for Annex I), the Regulation applies only if their design changes significantly from that date, and the first unit of the type and model sets the date (recital (39) of Regulation (EU) 2026/1744); the cut-off is no longer the fixed 2 August 2026. Legacy systems intended for use by public authorities comply by 2 August 2030 whatever their design changes; components of the Annex X large-scale IT systems placed on the market or put into service before 2 August 2027 sit outside Article 111(2) and comply by 31 December 2030 (Article 111(1)). Article 5 applies to legacy systems. Annex I Section B requires sectoral-route analysis under Article 2(2), rather than automatic direct Section 2 application. These rules are pending legal review (LR-03, LR-10).
applicationContext.sourceCurrencyRule: Source publication, research and application dates have different meanings. A new source version creates an impact-review candidate and never rewrites a historical decision.

decisionPolicy.providerResponsibility: Articles 9-15 are system requirements; provider responsibility is linked through Article 16(a). A deployer may inspect provider evidence but does not thereby assume every provider duty. Article 25 role changes need separate review.
decisionPolicy.dataScope: Under Article 10(1), datasets used for data-trained models are assessed; Article 10(6) limits Article 10(2)-(4) and Article 4a(1) to testing datasets for systems without model training. Article 10(5) was deleted; special-category processing is a separate Article 4a/data-protection assessment, not an upload permission. Article 4a(2) extends the same conditions and safeguards to providers and deployers of other AI systems and models and to deployers of high-risk systems, and creates no obligation to carry out bias detection and correction.
decisionPolicy.retention: Retention is actor, control, purpose and law dependent. Article 26(6) is not one universal evidence-vault retention policy.
decisionPolicy.excludedActorDuties: Other provider, deployer, representative, importer, distributor, sectoral, conformity, registration and fundamental-rights duties must be added where applicable. This selective catalog does not waive them.

factDerivations.rule: A derived fact is true if any listed fact is true, false if all are false, otherwise unknown (docs/research/art50-transparency-2026-11.json, vocabularies.derivationRule). Classification never asks a derived fact directly. For art50DisclosureApplies, the facts of a role the operator does not hold (provider: interactsDirectlyWithNaturalPersons, generatesSyntheticContent; deployer: the other three) count as false.

dateFacts: The rule pack's application-date predicates (templates/catalog.json, regulatorySnapshot.applicationDates) use eight facts: generatesSyntheticContent, placedOnMarketDate, highRiskRoute, firstPlacedOnMarketOrPutIntoServiceDate, significantDesignChangeOnOrAfterChapterIIIDate, intendedForUseByPublicAuthorities, annexXLargeScaleItComponent and gpaiModelPlacedOnMarketDate. The guided classification records each of them as true, false or unknown (dates as YYYY-MM-DD or unknown): highRiskRoute from the reviewed route and the Article 6(3) derogation, generatesSyntheticContent from the four modality facts. A predicate that reads an unknown fact yields needs_information.

exclusionType.exclusions: A triggered item is excluded when the ifAll list of any of its exclusions is true; if none is true and one is unknown, the item needs information. An exclusion takes effect only with fact values the independent classification review approved; exclusions with basis 'guidance' rest on non-binding guidelines and stay pending legal review.
exclusionType.exceptionsTestedPerItem: Decision of 6 November 2026 (option a): a statutory exception claimed under Article 50(1), (3) or (4) never excludes the item. It is tested per output, channel or deployment in fieldwork (the model is criterion A50-P-04B-C01: label present or exception supported), so the item stays a candidate.
exclusionType.followsItems: Article 50(5) governs only how the information owed under Article 50(1) to (4) is given, and the scope exclusions of Article 2(6) and 2(10) take the system out of the Regulation. An item with followsItems is evaluated only after its own trigger: it is a candidate when at least one listed item of a role the operator holds is a candidate; otherwise it needs information when one of them needs information; otherwise it is excluded when one of them is excluded (with that item's exclusion); otherwise it is not triggered.

triggerType.evaluation: Candidate selection only. Unknown in a required predicate yields needs_information. Legal-period approval and scope exclusions are separate human decisions.

provider_datasets.scopeNote: Apply the dataScope policy; an absent training dataset is not a blanket exemption from testing-data duties.

operator_role_change.scopeNote: Review branding, substantial modification and intended-purpose changes against Article 25(1), including relevant contractual qualifications. Do not automatically reassign provider duties.

provider_art50.scopeNote: Article 50 applies whatever the risk class (Article 50(6)); no high-risk confirmation is required.

deployer_art50.scopeNote: Article 50 applies whatever the risk class (Article 50(6)); no high-risk confirmation is required.

operator_art50.scopeNote: Article 50(5) attaches to the information duties of providers and deployers alike.

items.title: Children and vulnerable-group consideration
items.reviewNote: Assess whether adverse impacts are likely; do not omit this consideration merely because affected groups were not identified in the supplied dataset.

items.title: Pre-market and current technical documentation
items.reviewNote: Assess Annex IV elements and any lawful simplified form; the amendment also covers SMCs. A simplified submission uses the Commission's form, which notified bodies must accept (Article 11(1), second subparagraph, as replaced). A generated audit report is not automatically the provider's complete technical documentation.

items.title: Risk, monitoring and operation traceability
items.reviewNote: Platform activity and metric-execution logs are not substitutes for the audited system's operational events.

items.title: Purpose, validated performance and foreseeable risks
Output explanation and interpretation information
items.reviewNote: These subitems contain where-applicable qualifications; assess them explicitly. A SHAP plot alone is not evidence of deployer comprehension.

items.title: Log collection, storage and interpretation instructions
Biometric separate dual verification
items.reviewNote: Review proportionality exceptions for law enforcement, migration, border control and asylum under applicable Union/national law. This is audited-system oversight, not the audit platform's reviewer/signer workflow.

items.title: Contextual and AI-specific cybersecurity
items.reviewNote: Article 15(2) is a Commission benchmark-development provision, not a separate private-operator pass/fail obligation.

items.title: Development, architecture, data, tests and security
items.reviewNote: Point 2(g) calls for dated/signed responsible-person test reports; these are not supplied merely by an unsigned diagnostic output.

items.title: Actual EU declaration of conformity
items.reviewNote: Pending legal review (LR-02): Article 47 sits in Chapter III Section 5, which applies from the 2 August 2026 general date on the text, but the declaration attaches to high-risk systems whose obligations apply from 2 December 2027 (Annex III) or 2 August 2028 (Annex I).

items.title: Post-market evaluation and monitoring plan
items.reviewNote: Pending legal review (LR-02): Article 72 sits in Chapter IX, which applies from the 2 August 2026 general date on the text, but the plan attaches to high-risk systems whose obligations apply from 2 December 2027 (Annex III) or 2 August 2028 (Annex I).

Operational monitoring and risk/incident response
items.reviewNote: Assess triggering events, recipient/escalation duties and actor/sector exceptions; no notification is sent automatically by catalog selection.

items.title: Retention of controlled system logs
items.reviewNote: Purpose-appropriate period of at least six months unless applicable law provides otherwise; assess data-protection and financial-sector qualifications.

items.title: Notice to affected natural persons
items.reviewNote: Assess Annex III use and law-enforcement qualifications; Article 50 obligations remain separately applicable.
